import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the relevant columns
# Labor force participation rate (modeled ILO estimate) - Series Code: SL.TLF.TOTL.ZS
labor_productivity = df['Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)'].values

# School enrollment, primary (percentage gross) - Series Code: SE.PRM.ENRR
primary_enrollment = df['School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)'].values

# School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross) - Series Code: SE.SEC.ENRR
secondary_enrollment = df['School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)'].values

# Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth) - Series Code: NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG
export_growth = df['Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'].values

# Combine education levels into a single variable
education_levels = np.column_stack((primary_enrollment, secondary_enrollment))

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(education_levels, export_growth)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
intercept = model.intercept_

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import scipy.stats as stats

df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the correct Series Names for the variables
labor_productivity_series = 'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)'
primary_enrollment_series = 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)'
secondary_enrollment_series = 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)'
export_growth_series = 'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'

# Extract the years
years = df.columns[4:].tolist()

# Extract the values for the relevant indicators
labor_productivity = df[df['Series Name'] == labor_productivity_series][years].values[0]
primary_enrollment = df[df['Series Name'] == primary_enrollment_series][years].values[0]
secondary_enrollment = df[df['Series Name'] == secondary_enrollment_series][years].values[0]
export_growth = df[df['Series Name'] == export_growth_series][years].values[0]

# Check for NaN values in export_growth
nan_indices = np.isnan(export_growth)
export_growth_imputed = np.where(nan_indices, np.nanmean(export_growth), export_growth)

# Combine education levels into a single variable
education_levels = np.column_stack((primary_enrollment, secondary_enrollment))

# Perform linear regression
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(education_levels, export_growth_imputed)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
intercept = model.intercept_

# Calculate p-values for the coefficients
p_values = np.zeros(2)
for i in range(2):
    # Perform t-test for the coefficient
    t_stat = coefficients[i] / np.sqrt(model.score_ / (len(education_levels) - 2))
    p_values[i] = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(abs(t_stat), len(education_levels) - 2))

coefficients, p_values, intercept

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import scipy.stats as stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the correct Series Names for the variables
labor_productivity_series = 'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)'
primary_enrollment_series = 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)'
secondary_enrollment_series = 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)'
export_growth_series = 'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'

# Extract the years
years = df.columns[4:].tolist()

# Extract the values for the relevant indicators
labor_productivity = df[df['Series Name'] == labor_productivity_series][years].values[0]
primary_enrollment = df[df['Series Name'] == primary_enrollment_series][years].values[0]
secondary_enrollment = df[df['Series Name'] == secondary_enrollment_series][years].values[0]
export_growth = df[df['Series Name'] == export_growth_series][years].values[0]

# Check for NaN values in export_growth
nan_indices = np.isnan(export_growth)
export_growth_imputed = np.where(nan_indices, np.nanmean(export_growth), export_growth)

# Combine education levels into a single variable
education_levels = np.column_stack((primary_enrollment, secondary_enrollment))

# Perform linear regression
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(education_levels, export_growth_imputed)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
intercept = model.intercept_

# Calculate R-squared value
r_squared = model.score(education_levels, export_growth_imputed)

# Calculate standard error of the coefficients
n = len(education_levels)
k = education_levels.shape[1]
standard_error = np.sqrt((1 - r_squared) * (n - 1) / (n - k - 1) / np.diag(np.linalg.inv(education_levels.T @ education_levels)))

# Calculate t-statistics and p-values
t_statistics = coefficients / standard_error
p_values = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(abs(t_statistics), n - k - 1))

coefficients, p_values, intercept

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the correct Series Names for the variables
labor_productivity_series = 'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)'
primary_enrollment_series = 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)'
secondary_enrollment_series = 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)'
export_growth_series = 'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'

# Extract the years
years = df.columns[4:].tolist()

# Extract the values for the relevant indicators
labor_productivity = df[df['Series Name'] == labor_productivity_series][years].values[0]
primary_enrollment = df[df['Series Name'] == primary_enrollment_series][years].values[0]
secondary_enrollment = df[df['Series Name'] == secondary_enrollment_series][years].values[0]
export_growth = df[df['Series Name'] == export_growth_series][years].values[0]

# Check for NaN values in export_growth
nan_indices = np.isnan(export_growth)
export_growth_imputed = np.where(nan_indices, np.nanmean(export_growth), export_growth)

# Combine education levels into a single variable
education_levels = np.column_stack((primary_enrollment, secondary_enrollment))

# Reshape export_growth_imputed to be a 2D array
export_growth_imputed_2d = export_growth_imputed.reshape(-1, 1)

# Stack the arrays to form a single matrix
data_matrix = np.hstack((education_levels, export_growth_imputed_2d))

# Compute the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = np.corrcoef(data_matrix, rowvar=False)

# Visualize the correlation matrix
sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix, annot=True, fmt=".2f", xticklabels=['Primary Enrollment', 'Secondary Enrollment', 'Export Growth'], yticklabels=['Primary Enrollment', 'Secondary Enrollment', 'Export Growth'])
plt.show()
